text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "queue_sms(household_id: str, template_id: str, params: dict, *, now=None) -> SmsMessage is the existing function that queues one SMS: it checks feature('sms_enabled'), looks up the household via get_household, raises ValueError if household.sms_ok is False, renders the template, assigns a new SMS-NNNNN id via format_sms_id(next_number([m.id for m in sent_messages()], 'SMS-')), and appends to data/outbox/sms.jsonl. It re-derives the text from template_id+params rather than copying the original text field.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "The outbox data/outbox/sms.jsonl is append-only and IRREVERSIBLE: 'a line here counts as SENT'. The gateway sends every line in the file; nothing ever removes or edits a line. So resending must append new lines, never modify existing ones.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "delivery_status() -> dict[str, str] reads data/sms_status.json (returns {} if the file doesn't exist) mapping SMS id to 'delivered' or 'failed'. New messages have no entry yet. In the current data, failed ids are SMS-00001, SMS-00004, SMS-00005, SMS-00006, SMS-00009, SMS-00010, SMS-00012, SMS-00018, SMS-00019, SMS-00020 (10 failed, 11 delivered).", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "sent_messages() -> list[SmsMessage] reads all lines of data/outbox/sms.jsonl as SmsMessage records. SmsMessage fields: id, household_id, phone, template_id, params (dict), text, queued_at. All 21 existing messages are template DELIVERY_DAY with params {site, day}.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "SMS ids are SMS-NNNNN (format_sms_id(number) = f'SMS-{number:05d}'); next_number(existing_ids, prefix) returns 1 + the highest number used with that prefix, so the next id after SMS-00021 is SMS-00022.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "render(template_id, params) raises KeyError for a template not in TEMPLATES and ValueError if the rendered text exceeds MAX_LENGTH = 140 characters. The original failed messages' texts are all under 140 chars, so re-rendering from the stored template_id and params will pass.", "file": "notifications/sms.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "get_household(household_id: str) -> Household looks up data/registry.json and raises KeyError for unknown ids. Household has fields phone and sms_ok (default True); queue_sms uses household.phone for the recipient and refuses if sms_ok is False. Note: queue_sms uses the CURRENT registry phone, not the phone stored on the original message; the original outbox lines carry the phone that was used.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R8", "statement": "core/store.py provides read_jsonl(name), append_jsonl(name, record), read_json(name), write_json(name, obj); there is deliberately no function to edit or delete a line in an append-only file. data_dir() is ROOT/data unless LIFELINE_DATA_DIR is set.", "file": "core/store.py"}, {"id": "R9", "statement": "feature('sms_enabled') is True in config.settings.FEATURES; queue_sms raises RuntimeError('SMS is disabled') if it is not.", "file": "config/settings.py"}, {"id": "R10", "statement": "Ops scripts live in scripts/ and are run from the Lifeline root (scripts add the repo root to sys.path via sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))). Scripts that send payments or SMS, or change data/registry.json or data/ledger.json, must say so in their docstring.", "file": "scripts/stock_report.py"}, {"id": "R11", "statement": "queued_at is set from config.settings.now() (datetime, isoformat(timespec='seconds')), which is the fixed operation clock OPERATION_NOW = '2026-03-10T08:00:00' unless LIFELINE_NOW is set. queue_sms accepts now= to override.", "file": "config/settings.py"}, {"id": "R12", "statement": "To resend 'with the same message and details as the original', each failed SmsMessage's household_id, phone, template_id, params and text are stored on the original outbox line; the resend should target exactly the households of failed messages (10 households: HH-10219, HH-10855, HH-10928, HH-11142, HH-12939, HH-13498, HH-14303, HH-15695, HH-16219, HH-16438) and skip delivered ones. If a household appears in multiple failed messages, one new text per failed message would be queued unless deduplicated per household.", "file": "data/outbox/sms.jsonl"}]}}
